# Authored M3 known answers

These synthetic fixtures and expectations were specified on 2026-10-07 before examining any M3 producer output. `generate.py` encodes the source; it does not import the engine or compute musical expectations. `expectations.json` retains pitches, exact quarter lengths, independent source lanes, reference mode and expected observations. Each lane is an explicit separate part/voice; entries become consecutive source measures numbered from 1. Source durations use divisions 4. Chord arrays stay in one source lane. Rests and forward gaps remain distinct. MIDI positive/negative controls use separate source channels/tracks with 480 PPQN; no voice separation is implied.

Pair counts are C/E/K/S/F for fifths; octaves share C/E/K/S and use their separate expected flag count. Other checks use explicit test-authored counts at their semantic gates. A failed passing/neighbor recognition has no warning expectation. Missing key/order/range is skipped, and known unclassified collections are checked unknown. Runtime representation differences never change the authored musical answers.

`extra.py` adds separately authored boundary variants without regenerating earlier fixtures. It specifies held/reattacked/ornamented/invalid-tie sevenths, tie/inversion episodes, partial order, inspection-only range events, collective silence/gaps and MIDI tail controls. The two literal source transformations create unknown lower concert occupancy and conflicting source keys under an override. MIDI endings use exact 480-PPQN tails of 120/480/0 ticks; expected kinds are none/authentic/authentic in both modes. These source transformations were specified before their producer checks.
